name: Tasmania
region: Tasmania, island state south of the mainland
tagline: A wild, green island of mountains, beaches and ancient forest, with convict history, a bold art museum, Hobart's waterfront and some of the best food and drink in Australia.
highlight: The view of Wineglass Bay from the lookout, a perfect white crescent of sand between pink granite peaks.
shortDescription: Australia's island state: Hobart and MONA, Cradle Mountain, Freycinet and Wineglass Bay, Port Arthur, Bruny Island and a wilderness of national parks, with a superb food scene.
metaDescription: A Tasmania travel guide: Hobart, MONA, Salamanca Market, Cradle Mountain, Wineglass Bay, Port Arthur, Bruny Island, Tasmanian food and whisky, when to go and a six-day plan.
knownFor: Wilderness, Cradle Mountain, Wineglass Bay, MONA, food, convict history
goodFor: Hiking, wildlife, food, art, road trips

image.file: File:Cradle Mountain over Dove Lake, Tasmania.jpg
image.alt: Cradle Mountain reflected in Dove Lake in the Tasmanian wilderness

intro: Tasmania is an island about the size of Ireland, 240 km south of the Australian mainland across Bass Strait, and it has long been the country's most unspoilt and least visited state. Around a fifth of it is a World Heritage Area, with mountains, rainforest, wild rivers and beaches, and it is home to unusual animals including the Tasmanian devil, wombats and wallabies. The Palawa people have lived here for at least 40,000 years.

European settlement began in 1803, and the island was a major convict destination, with the notorious Port Arthur penal settlement and other sites now on the UNESCO Australian Convict Sites list. Hobart, on the Derwent River beneath Mount Wellington, is the capital and the second-oldest city in the country, with Georgian sandstone warehouses, a lively waterfront and a Saturday market at Salamanca Place.

In recent years the island has become a food and culture destination. The Museum of Old and New Art, MONA, opened in 2011 and changed the way people saw the state, and Tasmania's whisky, cool-climate wine, cheese, seafood and cider are all outstanding. But the wilderness is still the main attraction, with day walks and multi-day trails through spectacular scenery.

whyVisit.intro: Tasmania combines wild landscapes, food and history in one compact, walkable island.

points.title: World-class wilderness
points.text: Cradle Mountain, Freycinet and the south-west offer some of Australia's best walking.

points.title: MONA and Hobart
points.text: A provocative art museum, a lively waterfront and historic streets.

points.title: Food and drink
points.text: Oysters, cheese, whisky, cider and wine, at cellar doors and farm gates.

points.title: Convict heritage
points.text: Port Arthur and other sites tell a dark story.

points.title: Unique wildlife
points.text: Tasmanian devils, wombats, echidnas and wallabies are easily seen.

attractionsIntro: The island is best explored by car, with a base in Hobart and a loop through the east and north-west.

attractions.name: Hobart and Salamanca Place

image.alt: Stalls at the Salamanca Market in Hobart on a Saturday

attractions.text: The waterfront of the capital, with sandstone warehouses, Battery Point's old streets and the Saturday Salamanca Market, which sells produce and crafts.
attractions.tip: Go early to the market, and stay for lunch on the docks.

attractions.name: MONA

image.file: File:Museum of Old and New Art (MONA) - Hobart - 49142246651.jpg
image.alt: The Museum of Old and New Art, MONA, on the Derwent River near Hobart

attractions.text: A privately owned museum built into a sandstone cliff on the Derwent, with a provocative collection of ancient and contemporary art, a winery and a brewery. Reached by ferry from Hobart.
attractions.tip: Take the ferry, and allow at least three hours.

attractions.name: Mount Wellington (kunanyi)

image.file: File:Mount Wellington from Sandy Bay, Hobart Tasmania.jpg
image.alt: Mount Wellington rising above the suburbs of Hobart

attractions.text: The mountain that towers over Hobart, at 1,271 metres, with a road to the summit and views across the city and Derwent estuary. Its Aboriginal name is kunanyi.
attractions.tip: Bring warm clothes, as it is much colder at the top.

attractions.name: Port Arthur Historic Site

image.file: File:Port Arthur Guard Tower and Surrounds, Tasmania.jpg
image.alt: The ruins of the Port Arthur convict settlement, with the guard tower and lawns

attractions.text: The most famous convict site in Australia, a settlement of stone buildings and gardens on the Tasman Peninsula, an hour from Hobart. It is also the site of a 1996 massacre, which is commemorated with a memorial garden.

attractions.name: Freycinet and Wineglass Bay

image.file: File:Freycinet Wineglass Bay And Promise Bay.jpg
image.alt: The curved white sand of Wineglass Bay in Freycinet National Park

attractions.text: A national park on the east coast, with pink granite peaks and the perfect beach of Wineglass Bay, reached by a walk to the lookout in about an hour return.
attractions.tip: Continue down to the beach if you can.

attractions.name: Cradle Mountain and Dove Lake

image.file: File:Boat shed and Cradle Mountain at Dove Lake, Tas.jpg
image.alt: The boat shed at Dove Lake with Cradle Mountain behind

attractions.text: The dramatic peak in the north-west, with a lake circuit walk of about 2 hours, and the start of the Overland Track, a 65-km multi-day walk.
attractions.tip: Book the Overland Track well in advance.

attractions.name: Bruny Island

image.file: File:North view from The Neck lookout, Bruny Island, Tasmania.jpg
image.alt: The narrow sandy isthmus known as The Neck on Bruny Island

attractions.text: An island off the south of Hobart, reached by a short ferry, with oysters, cheese, chocolate, whisky, cliffs and wildlife.
attractions.tip: Take a day tour or drive yourself.

thingsToDoIntro: Tasmania is best for walking, eating and taking your time.

thingsToDo.title: Walk to Wineglass Bay
thingsToDo.text: A well-graded path to the lookout, and on to the beach.

thingsToDo.title: Spend a day at MONA
thingsToDo.text: See the art, eat and taste at the vineyard.

thingsToDo.title: See a Tasmanian devil
thingsToDo.text: Wildlife parks and sanctuaries let you see devils, wombats and other animals.

thingsToDo.title: Try the local whisky, cider and oysters
thingsToDo.text: Distilleries, cellar doors and farm gates offer tastings and fresh seafood.

thingsToDo.title: Walk part of the Overland Track
thingsToDo.text: Even a day walk from Cradle Mountain gives a taste of the wilderness.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Bay of Fires
thingsToDo.text: A coast of white sand, turquoise water and orange lichen-covered rocks in the north-east.

foodIntro: Tasmania punches above its weight in food and drink, with cold, clean waters and fertile land.

foods.name: Oysters and seafood
foods.text: Fresh oysters, scallops, salmon, abalone and rock lobster.
foods.whereToTry: Bruny Island, Hobart's waterfront and the east coast.

foods.name: Cheese
foods.text: Artisan cheeses from Bruny Island, King Island and northern dairies.

foods.name: Whisky
foods.text: Tasmanian whisky has won international awards.

foods.name: Cider and wine
foods.text: Cool-climate pinot noir, sparkling wine and cider, from the Huon Valley and Tamar Valley.

foods.name: Scallop pie
foods.text: A classic Tasmanian pie filled with scallops and a curry sauce.

foods.name: Leatherwood honey
foods.text: A distinctive honey from the native leatherwood tree.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Hobart as a base, with a few nights in Freycinet or Cradle Mountain.

areas.name: Hobart and Battery Point
areas.text: Hotels, boutique guesthouses and apartments near the waterfront.

areas.name: Freycinet and Coles Bay
areas.text: Cabins and lodges near the park.

areas.name: Cradle Mountain
areas.text: Lodges and cabins near the park entrance.

gettingThere.intro: Tasmania is reached by air or by ferry from Melbourne.

options.text: Direct flights from Melbourne (about 1 hour 20 minutes), Sydney and Brisbane.
The Spirit of Tasmania sails overnight from Geelong to Devonport, with cabins and vehicle space.
options.detail: Book cabins and vehicles well ahead.

options.text: The main way to explore, at a moderate cost.

gettingAround.intro: A car is essential for most of the island.

options.text: Roads are quiet and scenic, though winding.
options.detail: Avoid driving at dusk, when wallabies and wombats are active.

options.text: Day tours from Hobart cover Port Arthur, Bruny Island and Mount Wellington.
options.detail: Easy if you don't want to drive.

options.text: Ferries to MONA and Bruny Island.

bestTime.headline: December–March
bestTime.summary: Tasmania has a cool, changeable maritime climate. Summer is best for walking and beaches, and autumn is often clear and calm.

seasons.text: Long, mild days, ideal for walking. The busiest and most expensive time.
Settled weather, autumn colours and fewer people.
Cold and wet, with snow in the mountains and the Dark Mofo festival in June.
Variable, with wildflowers and green landscapes.

bestTime.avoid: Winter in the mountains, unless you are equipped, and Christmas week for prices.

itinerary.title: Six days in Tasmania
itinerary.intro: Hobart and its surroundings, then the east coast and Cradle Mountain.

tipsIntro: A few tips make Tasmania easier.
tips: Hire a car, and book it early in summer.
Pack layers. The weather changes quickly, even in summer.
Avoid driving at dusk and dawn, when wildlife is on the road.
Book Overland Track permits, the ferry and Freycinet accommodation well ahead.
Take a sunhat and rain jacket.
Buy a Parks Pass if visiting several national parks.
Leave time. The distances are small but the roads are winding.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Tasmania?
faq.a: At least five days, and a week is better.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: December to March, with autumn also lovely.
Yes. It has some of Australia's best scenery, food and history, and is relatively uncrowded.

faq.q: Can I see a Tasmanian devil?
faq.a: Yes, in wildlife parks and sanctuaries. Seeing one in the wild is rarer.
Yes, for most of the island.

faq.q: Can I take my car on the ferry?
faq.a: Yes, on the Spirit of Tasmania. Book well in advance.
